steps.path: Settings → Development → Developer tools on, then the X-ray button in the top bar
steps.headline: X-ray replaces the messages with every saved line of the session, in order, tagged with what normal chat did.
steps.changed: Each row is one line of the session's saved file: its number, time, what kind of line it is, a one-line summary, and on the right whether chat shows it, hides it or trims it. Hidden lines carry a coloured edge on the left. The message box and Stop button below still work.
steps.measured: 37 saved lines here; normal chat hides 9 and trims 1
steps.notice: The sample session is stuck re-running a failing test. 'Repeat ×2, ×3, ×4' marks each identical call, the '3 repeated calls — next' button jumps between them, and a line marks the 4-minute stall. The reminders and hook messages chat never showed sit in place, in order.
steps.risk: Built against made-up sample data so far. The part that reads a real session's file comes after you approve this look.

steps.headline: Clicking a row opens the line exactly as saved, with Copy line and a jump between a tool call and its result.
steps.changed: The open row shows the full saved text, laid out so it's readable, plus its size. A tool call offers 'Go to result', a result offers 'Go to call'. Copy line copies the exact saved text, to paste into a bug report or a fixing session.
steps.notice: This replaces opening the raw file by hand to see what the model actually sent.
steps.risk: Copied lines can contain private content from the conversation.

steps.headline: A 'Developer tools' switch at the bottom of Development turns the X-ray button on.
steps.changed: One new row under 'Get beta builds'. Off by default; while it's off, nobody sees an X-ray button anywhere. Turning it off returns every session to normal chat.
steps.notice: Desktop only for now: the row doesn't appear on the phone or in remote web.
steps.risk: The setting is per computer, so turning it on here doesn't turn it on elsewhere.

steps.path: The row of chips at the top of X-ray
steps.headline: Are these the right filters to start with?
steps.today: X-ray has four kind filters — Messages, Tools, Behind the scenes, Bookkeeping — plus 'Only hidden in chat' and a search box. With none lit, everything shows.
steps.problem: Too few filters and a long session is slow to narrow down; too many and the row becomes its own thing to learn.
steps.proposal: Keep these five and the search box. Yes keeps them; No or Other — tell me which to add or drop.

steps.path: X-ray on a session that uses the app's own assistant
steps.headline: For the app's own sessions, should X-ray also show what the app sends the model that isn't in the saved file?
steps.today: Claude Code sessions save almost everything the model sees, including hidden reminders. The app's own sessions (other models, local models) save only the conversation itself — the instructions and tool list sent with every request are rebuilt each time and never written down.
steps.problem: When one of the app's own sessions misbehaves, the cause can be in those unsaved instructions, and X-ray would have nothing to show for them.

options.label: Saved file only, for now
pros: The 'What the assistant was given' panel above the conversation already lists the instruction files.
cons: The tool list and the exact text sent each turn stay invisible in X-ray.

options.label: Record and show it too
pros: The complete picture of every request, in one place.
cons: The app would save a copy of the instructions with every turn, which takes disk space.
More work before X-ray is usable.
